title: Total Qty sort puts untracked parts below tracked parts in both directions
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919); the Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Part Library & Inventory → Create & Edit' and 'Part Library & Inventory → Delete' and can see costs and prices.
  • Parts → Inventory is open on the Active tab at {Location-A}.
  • Bin {Bin-A} is the default bin of {Location-A} (for example General Storage), the bin New Inventory Part fills in.
  • Five parts at {Location-A} have numbers starting {Prefix-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-SORTQ-), each with one bin, {Bin-A}, holding only a positive quantity.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-SORTQ-12, described ZZAUTOTEST PL SORTQ ALPHA) is tracked with 5 on hand.
  • Inventory part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-SORTQ-11, described ZZAUTOTEST PL SORTQ BRAVO) is tracked with 5 on hand.
  • Inventory part {Part-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-SORTQ-15, described ZZAUTOTEST PL SORTQ CHARLIE) is tracked with 2 on hand.
  • Inventory part {Part-D} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-SORTQ-14, described ZZAUTOTEST PL SORTQ XRAY) is untracked with 1 on the shelf.
  • Inventory part {Part-E} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-SORTQ-13, described ZZAUTOTEST PL SORTQ YANKEE) is untracked with 9 on the shelf.
  • The part numbers deliberately run against the descriptions, so a sort by number would give a different order.
  • {Prefix-A} is typed in the Inventory search.
custom_steps:
1. Click the Total Qty column header once.
  2. Read the five rows from top to bottom.
  3. Click the Total Qty header again.
  4. Read the five rows from top to bottom.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: The Total Qty column sorts; its header shows a sort arrow.
  • Step 2: Order: {Part-C} (2), {Part-A} (5), {Part-B} (5), {Part-D}, {Part-E}. Tracked parts go up by quantity (2 before 5); {Part-A} (ALPHA) comes before {Part-B} (BRAVO) because equal quantities are ordered by description A to Z; both untracked parts come after every tracked part, {Part-D} (XRAY) before {Part-E} (YANKEE) by description.
  • Step 4: Order: {Part-A} (5), {Part-B} (5), {Part-C} (2), {Part-D}, {Part-E}. Tracked parts go down by quantity; {Part-A} still comes before {Part-B}; the untracked parts are still last, still {Part-D} then {Part-E}, even though {Part-E} has 9 on the shelf.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10819 (Story 6, Search and Sort the Inventory List by Tracking State); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S6-R3, S6-R4, S6-R5, S6-R6, S6-R7, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 5.4 (Finding untracked parts) and tracking-note-3, 13 Oct copy. Tech plan Phase 5 notes the sort reads the stored quantity while the cell shows available stock, so this case uses parts with positive bins only. Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S6-R3: “The Total Qty column can be sorted.”
  • S6-R4: “When that column is sorted, untracked parts sit below every tracked part, in both sort directions.”
  • S6-R5: “Tracked parts sort against each other by quantity.”
  • S6-R6: “Tracked parts with the same quantity are then ordered by description, A to Z.”
  • S6-R7: “Untracked parts are ordered by description, A to Z.”
  • Tech plan Phase 5 (known gap): “Known pre-existing gap, not fixed here: the SQL sorts on `p.quantity`, while the cell shows the bin-derived available quantity.”
